newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Foods says fundamentals good.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Foods says fundamentals good.

text.p: Irish food group Waterford Foods Plc, who recently announced a profit warning, said on Monday the fundamentals of the business were sound and it was confident of a satisfactory outcome for 1997.
Waterford, on Tuesday last, said it expected 1996 pre-tax profits to be below current market expectations but not less than 19.7 million Irish pounds.
"The fundamentals of the business are sound and we are confident that the outturn for 1997 will be satisfactory," group managing director, Matt Walsh, said in a statement on Monday.
The group's share price plummeted 25 pence to 75 Irish pence immediately after the March 18 announcement. Waterford was quoted at 70/74 pence at 0935 GMT on Monday.
"As the Group has been the subject of intense media focus in recent days, I believe it is important to clarify some key points," Walsh said.
Walsh, who apologised to the Stock Exchange for the timing of the profit warning announcement, said he wished to emphasise that there was no difference of view between the Group and its auditors.

He said financial accounts were being prepared, certain assumptions and estimates were reviewed by management and discussed with the auditors, as a result of which the Board informed the market that the 1996 profit before taxation would be not less than 19.7 million Irish pounds.
"We have written to the Stock Exchange on this matter with the assurance that there will be no recurrence," Walsh said.
The Group said it was having discussions with its banks in relation to some aspects of its banking covenants and was confident that this matter will shortly be satisfactorily concluded.
